---
title: "From Dependence to Causality"
---

> **Status:** outline — to be filled out next.

Correlation (and even dependence) does not imply causation. This section covers what it
takes to put *arrows* on the graph.

## Outline

- **Conditional dependence** — removing edges in a graph; the chi-square test.
- **Hypothesis testing** — null vs. alternative, p-values, and the classic trap
  $P(\text{obs}\mid H) \neq P(H\mid\text{obs})$.
- **Directional measures** — directed information; Granger causality from temporal
  regression; causality-from-residuals under additive-noise models ($y=f(x)+n$ vs.
  $x=f(y)+n$).
